title: Subject pronouns with singular olla forms
summary: Omit minä or sinä when olen or olet makes the subject clear; keep hän in independent sentences.
objectives: Omit minä or sinä when olen or olet makes the subject clear; keep hän in independent sentences.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: The ending can identify the subject
paragraphs: Olen identifies minä and olet identifies sinä. Olen täällä still means “I am here”.
Keeping these pronouns is grammatical. When a task requests omission, practise the shorter sentence.

sections.title: Keep a clear third-person subject
paragraphs: On does not identify who the person is. Keep hän when no earlier context names that person.
This lesson uses independent beginner sentences with explicit third-person subjects.

steps: The ending in olen identifies first-person singular.

examples.english: He or she is at school.
steps: On is third person but does not identify who.
Keep hän because no earlier context names the person.
The pronoun can be omitted when the listener is clear.

commonMistakes: Follow an explicit instruction to omit the optional pronoun.
Keep the third-person subject clear in an independent sentence.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Notice who the sentence is about. Translate “Hän on turvassa nyt.” into English and recover the subject from the form.
acceptedAnswers: He or she is safe now.
practiceExercises.explanation: Hän remains explicit because a third-person olla form does not identify a unique person or group by itself.

sentenceExplanation.translation: He or she is safe now.

parts.role: subject: the person or people described by the sentence
parts.formation: subject pronoun; no ending is added

parts.role: verb: links the subject to the context
parts.formation: hän takes the present-tense form on

parts.role: context: tells the location or state
parts.formation: supplied as a complete fixed expression; no change is required

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Build “You are at work today.” Address one person; leave out sinä.
practiceExercises.explanation: Olet identifies the one listener, so sinä may be omitted.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: agreeing olla + context; optional subject omitted
